name: Databases
description: Storing and querying structured data reliably: the relational model, relational algebra, SQL, schema design and normalisation, transactions, and storage and indexing.

topics.name: The Relational Model
topics.summary: Data as relations with declared constraints — the idea that made databases a discipline.

subtopics.name: Relations, Tuples and Schemas
subtopics.summary: Tables as sets of tuples, attributes, domains and the schema/instance distinction.

objectives.text: Define a relation schema with attributes and domains
Distinguish a schema from an instance of that schema
Explain why a relation is a set and what that implies about duplicate rows

subtopics.name: Keys and Integrity Constraints
subtopics.summary: Candidate, primary and foreign keys, entity integrity and referential integrity.

objectives.text: Identify candidate keys for a relation and choose a primary key
Explain referential integrity and what a foreign key guarantees
State the effect of deleting a row that another table references

subtopics.name: Conceptual Modelling
subtopics.summary: Entities, attributes and relationships, and mapping an ER model to tables.

objectives.text: Draw an entity-relationship model for a described domain
Map one-to-many and many-to-many relationships to relational tables
Represent a weak entity and justify its key

topics.name: Relational Algebra
topics.summary: The formal operations a query engine actually executes, and the basis of query optimisation.

subtopics.name: Selection, Projection and Rename
subtopics.summary: Filtering rows, choosing columns, and why projection can remove duplicates.

objectives.text: Write selection and projection expressions for a stated query
Explain why projection may return fewer tuples than its input
Compose selection and projection and state the resulting schema

subtopics.name: Joins
subtopics.summary: Cartesian product, theta join, equijoin, natural join and outer joins.

objectives.text: Express a natural join as a product followed by selection and projection
Distinguish inner from left, right and full outer joins by their results
Predict the number of rows produced by a join

subtopics.name: Set Operations and Division
subtopics.summary: Union, intersection, difference, union compatibility, and 'for all' queries.

objectives.text: Apply union, intersection and difference to union-compatible relations
State the union compatibility requirement
Express a 'for all' query using division or a double negation

topics.name: SQL
topics.summary: The language every relational database speaks, and the one you will use most.

subtopics.name: Querying with SELECT
subtopics.summary: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, DISTINCT and predicate construction.

objectives.text: Write a SELECT statement with filtering and ordering for a stated requirement
Use DISTINCT correctly and explain its cost
Handle NULL correctly in a WHERE predicate

subtopics.name: Joins and Subqueries
subtopics.summary: Multi-table queries, correlated and uncorrelated subqueries, EXISTS and IN.

objectives.text: Write a multi-table query using explicit JOIN syntax
Distinguish a correlated from an uncorrelated subquery
Rewrite a subquery as a join where equivalent

subtopics.name: Aggregation and Grouping
subtopics.summary: COUNT, SUM, AVG, GROUP BY and HAVING, and how NULLs are treated.

objectives.text: Write a GROUP BY query with an aggregate and a HAVING filter
Explain the difference between WHERE and HAVING
State how aggregate functions treat NULL values

topics.name: Schema Design and Normalisation
topics.summary: Designing tables so that updating one fact requires changing exactly one place.

subtopics.name: Functional Dependencies
subtopics.summary: Determination between attribute sets, closure and the anomalies dependencies cause.

objectives.text: Identify functional dependencies from a described domain
Compute the closure of an attribute set
Explain insertion, update and deletion anomalies with an example

subtopics.name: Normal Forms
subtopics.summary: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF and BCNF, and decomposing a relation to reach them.

objectives.text: Determine the highest normal form a relation satisfies
Decompose a relation into 3NF, preserving dependencies
State the difference between 3NF and BCNF

subtopics.name: Denormalisation and Trade-offs
subtopics.summary: When redundancy is bought deliberately for read performance.

objectives.text: Explain why a fully normalised schema can perform poorly on reads
Describe a case where denormalisation is justified and its cost
Identify the update risk that denormalisation introduces

topics.name: Transactions
topics.summary: Keeping data correct when many users write at once and machines fail mid-write.

subtopics.name: ACID Properties
subtopics.summary: Atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability, and what each protects against.

objectives.text: Define each ACID property and the failure it guards against
Give an example where losing atomicity corrupts data
Explain what a transaction commit guarantees

subtopics.name: Concurrency Control
subtopics.summary: Interleaving anomalies, serialisability, locking and isolation levels.

objectives.text: Identify a lost update, dirty read or non-repeatable read in a schedule
Explain how two-phase locking achieves serialisability
Compare isolation levels by the anomalies each permits

subtopics.name: Recovery
subtopics.summary: Write-ahead logging, undo and redo, and restoring a consistent state after a crash.

objectives.text: Explain the write-ahead logging rule and why it is required
Describe how undo and redo restore consistency after a crash
State what must be durable before a commit can be acknowledged

topics.name: Storage and Indexing
topics.summary: Why a query is fast or slow — the physical layer beneath the relational abstraction.

subtopics.name: Files, Pages and Buffers
subtopics.summary: How rows are laid out on disk pages and cached in a buffer pool.

objectives.text: Explain how records are organised into pages and files
Describe the role of the buffer pool in reducing disk I/O
Estimate the pages read by a full table scan

subtopics.name: Indexes and B+ Trees
subtopics.summary: Clustered and secondary indexes, and why B+ trees suit disk-based storage.

objectives.text: Explain how a B+ tree index reduces lookup cost to logarithmic
Distinguish a clustered from a secondary index
State why B+ trees are shallow and wide rather than binary

subtopics.name: Query Performance
subtopics.summary: Reading a query plan and choosing indexes that actually get used.

objectives.text: Interpret a simple query plan and identify a full scan
Choose an index that supports a given query predicate
Explain why an index can slow down write-heavy workloads
